name: Missouri

law.statute: Missouri Revised Statutes § 196.298 (Cottage food production operation)
law.key_section: RSMo 196.298; related: RSMo 261.241 (jams/jellies/honey); Missouri Food Code food-establishment exemptions
regulations: Missouri Food Code (19 CSR / DHSS retail food code)

gate.regulator_primary: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services (DHSS)
gate.regulator_fallback: Local Public Health Agencies (complaint records; outbreak investigation; regulation outside cottage food)
gate.mechanism: A cottage food production operation under RSMo 196.298 is not a food service establishment and is not subject to state or local health or food code laws other than this section and cottage food rules. Local health departments shall not regulate cottage food production. No cottage food permit under this section.
gate.fee_notes: No permit fee under RSMo 196.298 cottage food path. Separate business licensing or tax registration may still apply outside the food statute.

prohibited_foods: Anything outside baked goods (non-PHF), canned jam or jelly, and dried herb or herb mix
Potentially hazardous baked goods (e.g. cream/meringue pies)
Sugar-free / no-sugar-added / hot-pepper jams or jellies that are potentially hazardous
Freeze-dried foods, salsa, pickles, sauces, cut produce, meats, dairy, eggs, pet foods (examples from DHSS guidance)
commodity_schemes: RSMo 261.241 jam/jelly/honey domicile exemption (US$30,000 cap) — separate from 196.298
Missouri Food Code individual-stand non-PHF exemption where local codes allow
scope.commodity_scheme_regulator: DHSS / LPHA / MDA depending on pathway

channels.render_reason: Statute centers on sale at the individual's home and DTC; internet only in-state; markets not named in 196.298
channels.notes: RSMo 196.298: produce for sale at individual's home; sell only directly to consumers. Internet only if both operation and purchaser in Missouri. Farmers markets not named in 196.298; Food Code stand exemption is a separate local pathway.

labelling.basis: RSMo 196.298(4); DHSS Home-Based Kitchen Food Production Guidance
required_elements: Name and address of the cottage food production operation
Statement that the food is not inspected by the department or local health department (statute)
Common name of the food (DHSS guidance)
Ingredients in descending order by weight (DHSS guidance)
labelling.mandated_disclaimer_text: This food is not inspected by the department or local health department. (RSMo 196.298(4) required statement content; DHSS guidance uses: product prepared in a kitchen not subject to inspection by DHSS.)
labelling.allergen_rule: DHSS cottage food label guidance includes listing any allergens

premises.inspection_frequency_basis: Local health and DHSS shall not regulate cottage food production under RSMo 196.298; complaint records maintained; outbreak investigation authority retained. Outside cottage food, LPHA/DHSS inspection may apply.
premises.construction_standard: Home means primary residence with a kitchen and appliances designed for common residential usage

unique.quirk_paragraph: Missouri looks open because RSMo 196.298 needs no permit and has no sales cap, but the product list is only three categories and the statute frames sale at the individual's home. Leave that path and local public health agencies matter again through the Missouri Food Code or local ordinances. A separate RSMo 261.241 jam/jelly/honey exemption still carries a US$30,000 cap. Internet cottage food sales are in-state only.
unique.common_mistake: Treating salsa, freeze-dried foods, or cream pies as cottage food, shipping out of state, wholesaling under 196.298, or confusing 196.298 with the Food Code stand exemption or RSMo 261.241.
unique.what_does_not_apply: Foods outside baked goods, canned jam/jelly, and dried herbs/herb mixes; wholesale; internet sales where buyer or seller is outside Missouri; assumption that every homemade non-PHF food is statewide cottage food.

information_gain: Only three product categories under RSMo 196.298
No sales cap in current 196.298; former US$50,000 cap removed 28 Aug 2022
Local health may not regulate cottage food production; complaint and outbreak authority retained
Internet only if both parties in Missouri
Separate pathways: Food Code local stand exemption and RSMo 261.241 (US$30,000 jam/jelly/honey)
Statute sale-at-home framing; markets not named in 196.298
